2. In original plaint. it is stated that, suit land originally belonged to Ainuddin Hayder and Faizunnessa Bibi Waif Estate, who made Waqf of the property by Waqf deed No. 30 dated 23.04.1864 and deed No. 373 dated 04.02.1877. Ahsanullah Khan Bahadur was one of the Mutwalli of this Waqf Estate and in cronological way, the members of the Nawab Family became Mutwalli and last Mutwalli was Nawab Khawja Hassan Askari, who was Mutwalli up to 1974. When cadastral survey started, this Waqf property as per deed and on the basis of Mutwalli, was included in the name of Nawab Courts of Wards represented by Nawab Sir Salimullah although as per record, it ought to be recorded in the name of Ainuddin Hayder and Faizunnessa Bibi Waqf Estate. When Nawab Khawja Habibullah was Mutwalli, he, as per section 44 of the Waqf Ordinance, by application dated 22.05.1934, enrolled the property as E.C. No. 411/C. Nawab Sir Salimullah while Mutwalli of Ainuddin Hayder and Faizunnessa Bibi Waqf Estate, died leaving son, Nawab Khawja Habibullah. Nawab Khawja Habibullah died leaving son. Nawab Khawja Hasan Askari who continue as, Mutwalli till S.A. and R.S. survey started but due to mismanagement it was recorded in the name of lessee in S.A. and R.S. 

 well as in respect of title of the property of Waqf in favour of Waqf Estate. The suit was decreed against Nawab Sir Salimullah and others. Against which Nawab Sir Salimullah filed Appeal No. 389 of 1909 before the High Court Division at Calcutta and on contesting hearing the appeal was allowed on 30.08.1909 and in the judgment it is opined that Nawab Sir Salimullah for his live time would he the Mutwalli of Ainuddin Hayden and Faizunnessa Waqf Estate and plaintiff of that suit, Abul Khali Md. Mostfa or their heirs will never became the Mutwalli of the Estate. This Waqf Estate originally was for a vast property and the some of the land are managed by the Nawab Courts of Wards as C.S. khatian and C.A. roll recorded the name of Courts of Wards. Plaintiff filed case before the court of Settlement Dhaka under section 50 of the State Acquisition of Tenancy Act for correction and by order dated 27.04.1975 the C.A. roll recorded the name of Faizunnessa Bibi Waqf Estate but Mutwalliship was not corrected. Papers having not been collected earlier, the suit could not be filed earlier. Wagf Administrator in Memo -No. Ao: 0: Pro:/141 Dha: Da: dated 17.09.2001 gave permission to lessee Md. Kamrul Hasan for Netter interest of the Waqf Estate, for better interest of Ainuddin Hayder and Faizunnessa E.C. No. 41 11 C to continue the suit. On 27.05.1990 the Estate filed application to Mutwalli of Bangladesh Wag Administrator, Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka for correction of record by Memo No. 698/Dhaka dated 07.06.1991) with written request to Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka to cornea the record. Defendant Nos. I and 2 disclosed that they have purchased the suit land from defendant No. 3 to which plaintiff demanded purchase deed from defendant No.1 and 2 but they did not. As per paragraph No. 2 of the Waqf deed it has been slated that no lease can be sustainable for any period beyond 3 years: lease deed of defendant was for 3 years, as such defendant Nos. 3.4 has no right, title to settle the suit property.
